accepted.question_text: Let sum_{n=0}^{infinity} a_n be a conditionally divergent series of real numbers, and let S = {L in R : L = sum_{n=0}^{infinity} a_{sigma(n)} for some lambda-permutation sigma}. A lambda-permutation is, when applied to the index of a series, convergence-preserving and "fixing" at least one divergent series. Can S ever be something between empty set and R?

evidence.quote: In 2006, another mathematician Daniel Velleman raised an open problem related to λ-permutation: for a conditionally divergent series P∞ n=0 an, n ∈ N, an ∈ R, let S = {L ∈ R: L = P∞ n=0 aσ(n) for some λ-permutation σ}, can S ever be something between ∅ and R?
This type of permutation, when applied to the index of terms of series, is defined to be both convergence-preserving and "fixing" at least one divergent series

needs_review.question_text_raw: Moving forward from type R lambda-permutation, it will be helpful to incrementally relax the constraint it imposes on general lambda-permutation to progress toward the original Velleman's problem. Some ideas include out-of-order selection of elements within a positive/negative block, out-of-order selection of a finite number of same-sign blocks, and combining the above two.
